title: Beyond the 956: JoBe Cerny, voice of the Pillsbury Doughboy, dies at 78
excerpt: JoBe Cerny, the actor who voiced the Pillsbury Doughboy from 2014 to 2020, died October 30, 2026, at 78 in Grayslake, Illinois, after a battle with Alzheimer's disease.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

JoBe Cerny, the actor whose giggle gave voice to the Pillsbury Doughboy, has died at 78.

Cerny died Friday, October 30, 2026, in Grayslake, Illinois, following a battle with Alzheimer’s disease, his family announced in his obituary. He was 78. His son, Tim Cerny, confirmed the news to TMZ, saying his father was diagnosed with Alzheimer’s around 2020 and stepped away from voicing the Doughboy as his health declined.

Born December 5, 1947, in Cicero, Illinois, Cerny got his distinctive first name by combining his parents’ names, Joe and Bea. He earned a bachelor’s degree in speech and drama from Valparaiso University and a master’s degree in theater from Northwestern University. In the 1970s he joined Chicago’s legendary Second City comedy theater, performing with both the Mainstage and the National Touring Company.

Cerny voiced the Pillsbury Doughboy — Poppin’ Fresh, the little baker who giggles when someone pokes his belly — from 2014 to 2020, succeeding Paul Frees and Jeff Bergman in the role. He was also Procter & Gamble’s silent spokesman for Cheer detergent, the Cheer Man. On screen, he appeared in Somewhere in Time, My Best Friend’s Wedding, Road to Perdition, and Legally Blonde 2: Red, White & Blonde.

He owned and operated Cerny/American Creative Recording Studio in Chicago’s River North neighborhood for more than 30 years, and directed The Word of Promise, a 98-hour audio production of the New King James Version of the Bible featuring more than 500 actors.

Cerny is survived by his wife of 56 years, Eileen Cerny; his sons, Tim and Patrick; his daughters-in-law, Andrea and Lily; and his grandchildren, Archer and Cleo. A private service was held for immediate family.

Rest in Peace, JoBe Cerny.

Sources: USA TODAY (November 10, 2026); The Wrap (November 10, 2026); family obituary, Strang Funeral Chapel, Grayslake, Illinois.
